Enumeration representing byte order for EXIF data: Motorola for big-endian and Intel for little-endian. Used to select how multi-byte values are encoded/decoded when reading or writing EXIF structures. Details beyond the two values are not provided in this header.

Enumeration indicating the image data type to which EXIF metadata applies. Values include several uncompressed layouts, a compressed type, a count sentinel, and an alias UNKNOWN equal to COUNT. Used to select constraints/interpretation rules for EXIF tags based on image data format. Destruction/ownership do not apply (plain enum).

objects.description: Enumeration of native EXIF tag data formats as defined by the EXIF specification. Values correspond to the numeric EXIF format codes. Used to identify the storage type of tag data (e.g., BYTE, ASCII, SHORT, LONG, RATIONAL, signed variants, and floating-point types).

Enumeration of possible EXIF Image File Directories (IFDs). Values identify the primary IFD (0), the secondary/thumbnail IFD (1), the EXIF-specific IFD, the GPS IFD, the Interoperability IFD, and a sentinel EXIF_IFD_COUNT used as a size/count marker rather than a real IFD. Useful for selecting or iterating IFDs in EXIF metadata processing.

Opaque logging context used by libexif’s logging infrastructure. The structure is forward-declared here and defined elsewhere; it is reference-counted via exif_log_ref/unref and freed with exif_log_free. Details of its internal fields are not exposed in this header.

objects.description: Enumeration of EXIF tag IDs used in TIFF/EXIF metadata. Each enumerator maps a symbolic name to its numeric tag identifier. Used throughout libexif for identifying tags.
Enumeration describing the level of support a tag has in a given IFD and data type per the EXIF specification.

Function pointer type for an allocator that behaves like calloc: allocates a block of size s and returns a zero-initialized pointer. Exact initialization semantics are implied by comment but not enforceable in type. ExifLong is defined elsewhere. Used to supply custom allocation to ExifMem.

Function pointer type for a reallocator that behaves like realloc: resizes the block pointed to by p to size s and returns the (possibly moved) pointer. ExifLong is defined elsewhere. Used by ExifMem for custom reallocation.
Function pointer type for a deallocator that frees the memory at p. Intended to match free-like semantics. Used by ExifMem for custom deallocation.

Opaque handle to the library’s memory manager. Actual struct definition is hidden (forward declaration only). Instances are created with exif_mem_new or exif_mem_new_default, reference-counted with exif_mem_ref/unref, and used to allocate, reallocate, and free memory through exif_mem_alloc/realloc/free which dispatch to the configured function pointers.

Opaque-manageable struct representing the set of EXIF entries (tags) contained in a single IFD. Holds an array of ExifEntry pointers, the number of entries, a back-pointer to the parent ExifData, and a pointer to private implementation data. Constructors and refcounting are provided by the API; clients should not free fields directly.

Function pointer type for iterating over each ExifEntry within an ExifContent. Callback receives the entry and a user_data pointer.

functions.name: exif_byte_order_get_name
functions.description: Returns a short, localized textual name for the specified Exif byte order. Typical usage: pass EXIF_BYTE_ORDER_MOTOROLA (big-endian) or EXIF_BYTE_ORDER_INTEL (little-endian) and receive a locale-dependent string; returns NULL if the value is not recognized. The returned pointer refers to read-only storage.
requirements: Parameter order must be a valid ExifByteOrder enumeration value (e.g., EXIF_BYTE_ORDER_MOTOROLA or EXIF_BYTE_ORDER_INTEL).
Caller must check for and handle a NULL return value (unknown or unsupported byte order).
The returned string is const; do not modify it.
Do not attempt to free the returned pointer (inferred from const char* and typical get_name pattern).

functions.name: exif_format_get_name
functions.description: Returns a localized textual name for the specified EXIF data type. Use this to map an ExifFormat enum value to a human-readable string for logging, UI, or diagnostics. If the format is unknown, the function returns NULL. The returned string is const-qualified and intended to be read-only; typical usage is to check for NULL and then use the string without modification.
requirements: The format argument should be a valid ExifFormat enum value.
Callers must check the return value for NULL before dereferencing or using it (unknown formats yield NULL).
The returned string is const; callers must not modify it.
Ownership/ lifetime of the returned pointer is not specified in this header; callers should not attempt to free it.

functions.name: exif_format_get_size
functions.description: Returns the raw size, in bytes, of a single component of the specified EXIF data type. This lets callers compute storage sizes for tag values of a given format. Behavior for unknown or invalid formats is not specified in this header.
requirements: The format argument should be a valid ExifFormat enum value.
Callers should treat the return as the size in bytes of one element of the given format.
Behavior for unknown/invalid formats is unspecified; callers should be prepared to handle any value representable by unsigned char.

functions.name: exif_ifd_get_name
functions.description: Returns a textual name for the specified EXIF Image File Directory (IFD). The name is a short, unique, non-localized US-ASCII alphanumeric string. Use this to obtain a human-stable identifier (not localized) for an ExifIfd value. Returns NULL if the IFD is unknown.
requirements: Parameter ifd should be a valid ExifIfd enum value (e.g., EXIF_IFD_0, EXIF_IFD_EXIF, etc.).
Caller must handle a NULL return value (returned when the IFD is unknown).
The returned pointer refers to a const string; the caller must not modify or free it.

functions.name: exif_log_new
functions.description: Create a new logging instance (an ExifLog object) using the library’s default memory allocator. Use exif_log_free or exif_log_unref to release it when done. Intended as the primary constructor for logging state used with other exif_log* APIs.
requirements: Caller must release the returned ExifLog using exif_log_free or exif_log_unref to avoid leaks.
The returned pointer must be treated as an opaque handle and only used with this API.

functions.name: exif_log_new_mem
functions.description: Create a new logging instance using the provided ExifMem allocator. This is a variant of exif_log_new that binds the instance to a specific memory manager for allocations.
requirements: The ExifMem* argument must refer to a valid, initialized ExifMem allocator object from libexif (exact initialization details are defined in exif-mem.h).
Caller must release the returned ExifLog using exif_log_free or exif_log_unref to avoid leaks.

functions.name: exif_log_ref
functions.description: Increase the reference count of an ExifLog instance. Use to hold an additional reference when sharing the logger across components.
requirements: log must be a valid ExifLog pointer previously created by exif_log_new or exif_log_new_mem and not already freed/unref’d to zero.
Each successful exif_log_ref should be balanced with a corresponding exif_log_unref.

functions.name: exif_log_unref
functions.description: Decrease the reference count of an ExifLog instance. When the count reaches zero, the instance is destroyed. Prefer this over exif_log_free when using reference counting.
requirements: log must be a valid ExifLog pointer previously created by exif_log_new or exif_log_new_mem and currently referenced.
Do not use the ExifLog after its reference count reaches zero (i.e., after the final unref).
Each exif_log_ref taken must be matched by an exif_log_unref.

functions.name: exif_log_free
functions.description: Delete (destroy) an ExifLog instance. This is the destructor counterpart to exif_log_new/exif_log_new_mem. Note: The comment in the header that says it returns a new instance is an apparent documentation error; it returns void.
requirements: log must be a valid ExifLog pointer created by exif_log_new or exif_log_new_mem.
After calling exif_log_free, the pointer must not be used again.
If reference counting is used, ensure this is only called when appropriate for your ownership model (or use exif_log_unref to balance refs).

functions.name: exif_log_code_get_title
functions.description: Return a short textual description (title) for a given logging message class (ExifLogCode). Returns NULL if the code is unknown.
requirements: The ExifLogCode value should be one of the defined enum constants (e.g., EXIF_LOG_CODE_NONE, EXIF_LOG_CODE_DEBUG, EXIF_LOG_CODE_NO_MEMORY, EXIF_LOG_CODE_CORRUPT_DATA).
Caller must handle a NULL return (unknown code).
The returned pointer is owned by the library and must not be freed or modified.

functions.name: exif_log_code_get_message
functions.description: Return a verbose description (message) for a given logging message class (ExifLogCode). Returns NULL if the code is unknown.
requirements: The ExifLogCode value should be one of the defined enum constants.
Caller must handle a NULL return (unknown code).
The returned pointer is owned by the library and must not be freed or modified.

functions.name: exif_log_set_func
functions.description: Register a log callback for the given ExifLog. Subsequent diagnostic log events are delivered to the callback with the provided user data. Calls are for diagnostics only.
requirements: log must be a valid ExifLog pointer.
func must be a function matching ExifLogFunc: void (*)(ExifLog *log, ExifLogCode, const char *domain, const char *format, va_list args, void *data).
The callback must be prepared to receive a printf-style format string with a corresponding va_list (do not use the variadic arguments directly; use the provided va_list).
data is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; its lifetime/ownership is managed by the caller.

functions.name: exif_log
functions.signature: void exif_log(ExifLog *log, ExifLogCode, const char *domain, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Emit a diagnostic log message to the ExifLog using a printf-style format and variadic arguments. Note: If NO_VERBOSE_TAG_STRINGS is defined at build time, exif_log may be compiled to a no-op macro instead of a function.
requirements: log must be a valid ExifLog pointer.

format must be a valid printf-style format string; the variadic arguments must match the format in type and count (the function is annotated with GCC printf-format checking: __attribute__((format(printf,4,5)))).
If exif_log is compiled as a macro no-op (when NO_VERBOSE_TAG_STRINGS is defined), calls will do nothing; callers should not rely on side effects in arguments beyond evaluation.

functions.name: exif_logv
functions.signature: void exif_logv(ExifLog *log, ExifLogCode, const char *domain, const char *format, va_list args);
functions.description: Variant of exif_log that takes a pre-built va_list for the message arguments. Useful when forwarding variadic arguments from another variadic function.
requirements: log must be a valid ExifLog pointer.
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
args must be an initialized va_list that matches the format string contents; its lifetime must extend through the call (per C varargs rules).

functions.name: exif_tag_from_name
functions.description: Maps a unique textual EXIF tag name to its numeric ExifTag ID. Intended for looking up a tag enum value by name when parsing or handling EXIF metadata. Returns 0 if the tag name is not found; note that 0 cannot be distinguished from a legitimate tag number 0.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid NUL-terminated C string for name; behavior for NULL or non-NUL-terminated input is unknown.
Caller must handle the case where the return value is 0 (tag not found), which is ambiguous with legitimate tag number 0 as noted in the header.

functions.name: exif_tag_get_name_in_ifd
functions.description: Returns the short, unique, non-localized US-ASCII alphanumeric name of the specified EXIF tag when it appears in the specified IFD. Use this for stable programmatic identifiers of tags. Returns NULL if the tag is unknown in that IFD.
requirements: Caller must pass a valid ExifTag value and a valid ExifIfd identifying the IFD of interest.
Caller must handle a NULL return value indicating the tag is unknown in the given IFD.
The returned pointer refers to library-managed memory that must not be modified or freed by the caller (implied by const char* typical API; ownership details otherwise unknown).

functions.name: exif_tag_get_title_in_ifd
functions.description: Returns a short, localized human-readable title for the specified EXIF tag when found in the specified IFD. Useful for UI display. Returns NULL if the tag is unknown in that IFD.
requirements: Caller must pass a valid ExifTag and ExifIfd.
Caller must handle a NULL return value indicating the tag is unknown in the given IFD.
The returned string is managed by the library and must not be modified or freed by the caller (implied by const; ownership otherwise unknown).

functions.name: exif_tag_get_description_in_ifd
functions.description: Returns a verbose, localized description of the specified EXIF tag when present in the specified IFD. Suitable for tooltips or documentation display. Returns NULL if the tag is unknown in that IFD.
requirements: Caller must pass a valid ExifTag and ExifIfd.
Caller must handle a NULL return value indicating the tag is unknown in the given IFD.
The returned string is managed by the library and must not be modified or freed by the caller (implied by const; ownership otherwise unknown).

functions.name: exif_tag_get_support_level_in_ifd
functions.signature: ExifSupportLevel exif_tag_get_support_level_in_ifd(ExifTag tag, ExifIfd ifd, ExifDataType t);
functions.description: Reports the EXIF standard support level of a tag in a given IFD and data type (unknown, not recorded, mandatory, optional). If ifd is EXIF_IFD_COUNT the result is EXIF_SUPPORT_LEVEL_UNKNOWN. If t is EXIF_DATA_TYPE_UNKNOWN the result is EXIF_SUPPORT_LEVEL_UNKNOWN unless the support level is the same for all data types.
requirements: Caller must pass a valid ExifTag.
ifd may be a specific IFD or EXIF_IFD_COUNT (which yields EXIF_SUPPORT_LEVEL_UNKNOWN).
t may be a specific ExifDataType or EXIF_DATA_TYPE_UNKNOWN (which typically yields EXIF_SUPPORT_LEVEL_UNKNOWN unless uniform across types).
Caller must handle any returned ExifSupportLevel value, including EXIF_SUPPORT_LEVEL_UNKNOWN.

functions.name: exif_tag_get_name
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns the short, unique, non-localized name of the tag without considering IFD. Use exif_tag_get_name_in_ifd instead. Returns NULL if the tag is unknown.
requirements: Caller should prefer exif_tag_get_name_in_ifd; this function is kept for compatibility.
Caller must handle a NULL return value indicating an unknown tag.
The returned string is library-managed; do not modify or free (implied by const; ownership otherwise unknown).

functions.name: exif_tag_get_title
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns a localized short title for the tag without considering IFD. Use exif_tag_get_title_in_ifd instead. Returns NULL if the tag is unknown.
requirements: Caller should prefer exif_tag_get_title_in_ifd; this function is kept for compatibility.

# The stub uses a fixed format string "%s %d %u" internally, but FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# is used twice: once for the domain and once for the string argument (sarg).
# Our generator should therefore return bytes that, when used as initial corpus
# for FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME, provide interesting but valid ASCII
# strings commonly seen as log domains or message fragments. We also include
# multiple NUL-terminated strings in one buffer to seed different extractions.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a sequence of NUL-terminated strings concatenated together in one
#   bytes blob. Fuzz harnesses often split on NULs to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# - Include realistic domains ("exif", "gps", etc.), path-like tokens, UTF-8
#   edge cases (still valid), and varying lengths (short, medium, near 1KB).
# - Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic given a seed but with randomness for variety.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

COMMON_DOMAINS = [
    "exif", "exif.loader", "exif.data", "exif.mnote", "gps", "ifd0", "ifd1",
    "exif-io", "libexif", "thumbnail", "maker", "interp", "tiff", "jpeg",
]

COMMON_WORDS = [
    "ok", "warn", "error", "debug", "info", "alloc", "free", "load", "save",
    "parse", "fix", "spec", "endianness", "big", "little", "intel", "motorola",
    "tag", "ifd", "gps", "exif", "rational", "short", "long",
]

UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "π", "æ", "✓", "©", "™", "—", "å", "ø", "č", "Ж", "漢字",
]

PATHS = [
    "/DCIM/100CANON/IMG_0001.JPG", "/photos/holidays/exif.jpg", "C:/Images/test.jpg",
    "./relative/path.jpg", "../updir/file.jpeg",
]

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:+#@[](){}",  # tuple
    # alphabet was a tuple due to trailing comma; fix:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:+#@[](){}"
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _domain_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = r.choice(COMMON_DOMAINS)
    # Optionally append subcomponents
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 2)):
        base += "." + _rand_ascii(r, 3, 8)
    return base

def _message_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Start with a common word
    parts.append(r.choice(COMMON_WORDS))
    # Mix in numbers and words
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
        choice = r.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(str(r.randint(-100000, 100000)))
        elif choice == 1:
            parts.append(hex(r.getrandbits(32)))
        elif choice == 2:
            parts.append(r.choice(COMMON_WORDS))
        elif choice == 3:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 2, 6))
        else:
            parts.append(r.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS))
    # Optionally add a path
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(r.choice(PATHS))
    return ' '.join(parts)

def _make_strings(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    strings: List[bytes] = []

    # Include an empty string to seed edge cases
    strings.append(b"")

    # Format string matching the stub arguments (valid and safe)
    strings.append(b"%s %d %u")

    # Some domain-like strings
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        strings.append(_domain_like(r).encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))

    # Some message-like strings
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 7)):
        strings.append(_message_like(r).encode('utf-8'))

    # Long message near 1KB
    long_parts = [_message_like(r) for _ in range(60)]
    long_msg = ' | '.join(long_parts)
    long_b = long_msg.encode('utf-8')[:1024]
    strings.append(long_b)

    # Path strings
    for p in PATHS:
        strings.append(p.encode('utf-8'))

    # Random ASCII blobs of varying sizes
    for size in [1, 8, 32, 128, 512]:
        strings.append(_rand_ascii(r, size, size).encode('ascii'))

    return strings

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    chunks = _make_strings(r)

    # Concatenate as NUL-terminated strings; final NUL ensures clean parsing
    out = bytearray()
    for s in chunks:
        # ensure no interior NULs except terminator for each string
        s = s.replace(b"\x00", b"")
        out += s + b"\x00"

    # Trim to maximum allowed size
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # Ensure buffer ends with NUL terminator
        if out[-1] != 0:
            # Backtrack to nearest earlier NUL or append one if space
            try:
                last_nul = out.rindex(0)
                out = out[:last_nul+1]
            except ValueError:
                # No NUL inside; ensure final byte is NUL
                out[-1] = 0

    return bytes(out)

    return r.randint(a, b)

def _choice(r: random.Random, seq: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    return r.choice(seq)

# JPEG/EXIF builder (APP1 with TIFF header and minimal IFD)
# Produces a minimal but valid EXIF APP1 segment that many parsers accept.
# Layout:
#  SOI FF D8
#  APP1 FF E1 [2-byte len]
#   "Exif\x00\x00"
#   TIFF header: byte order (II/MM), 0x002A, IFD0 offset
#   IFD0 with a few entries and proper next-IFD = 0
#   Value/data area for entries that don't fit in 4 bytes

def _build_tiff_header(order: str, ifd0_offset: int) -> bytes:
    if order == 'II':
        endian = b'II'
        pack16 = lambda v: struct.pack('<H', v)
        pack32 = lambda v: struct.pack('<I', v)
    else:
        endian = b'MM'
        pack16 = lambda v: struct.pack('>H', v)
        pack32 = lambda v: struct.pack('>I', v)
    return endian + pack16(0x002A) + pack32(ifd0_offset)

def _pack_ifd_entry(order: str, tag: int, fmt: int, count: int, value_or_offset: int | bytes) -> bytes:
    # IFD entry is 12 bytes: tag(2), format(2), count(4), value/offset(4)
    if order == 'II':
        p16 = lambda v: struct.pack('<H', v)
        p32 = lambda v: struct.pack('<I', v)
    else:
        p16 = lambda v: struct.pack('>H', v)
        p32 = lambda v: struct.pack('>I', v)
    entry = p16(tag) + p16(fmt) + p32(count)
    if isinstance(value_or_offset, bytes):
        # fit exactly 4 bytes
        v = value_or_offset.ljust(4, b'\x00')[:4]
        entry += v
    else:
        entry += p32(int(value_or_offset))
    return entry

def _build_min_exif(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose byte order
    order = 'II' if _rand(r, 0, 1) == 1 else 'MM'

    # Start building TIFF payload after "Exif\0\0"
    # We'll assemble TIFF as: [TIFF hdr][IFD0][value area]
    # IFD0 will have 3-5 entries among common tags
    entries = []
    value_area = bytearray()

    # Helper to add entry, returning potential offset placement
    def add_ascii(tag: int, text: bytes):
        # EXIF ASCII format = 2, must be NUL-terminated
        s = text + (b'\x00' if not text.endswith(b'\x00') else b'')
        fmt = 2
        count = len(s)
        if count <= 4:
            entries.append(_pack_ifd_entry(order, tag, fmt, count, s.ljust(4, b'\x00')))
        else:
            offset = None  # to be filled later with absolute offset
            # reserve space and record backpatch
            start = len(value_area)
            value_area.extend(s)
            entries.append((tag, fmt, count, start))

    def add_short(tag: int, value: int):
        # format SHORT=3, count=1
        fmt = 3
        count = 1
        if order == 'II':
            packed = struct.pack('<H', value) + b'\x00\x00'
        else:
            packed = struct.pack('>H', value) + b'\x00\x00'
        entries.append(_pack_ifd_entry(order, tag, fmt, count, packed))

    def add_rational(tag: int, num: int, den: int):
        fmt = 5  # RATIONAL
        count = 1
        start = len(value_area)
        if order == 'II':
            value_area.extend(struct.pack('<I', num))
            value_area.extend(struct.pack('<I', den))
        else:
            value_area.extend(struct.pack('>I', num))
            value_area.extend(struct.pack('>I', den))
        entries.append((tag, fmt, count, start))

    # Populate a few common tags
    # ImageWidth (0x0100) and ImageLength (0x0101) as SHORT within 4-bytes
    add_short(0x0100, _rand(r, 16, 4000))
    add_short(0x0101, _rand(r, 16, 4000))
    # Orientation (0x0112) 1..8
    add_short(0x0112, _choice(r, [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]))
    # Make and Model strings
    makes = [b"Canon", b"Nikon", b"Sony", b"Apple", b"GoPro", b"Panasonic", b"FUJIFILM"]
    models = [b"EOS", b"D750", b"iPhone", b"A7", b"HERO", b"Lumix", b"X-T3"]
    add_ascii(0x010F, _choice(r, makes))
    add_ascii(0x0110, _choice(r, models))
    # XResolution/YResolution RATIONAL
    add_rational(0x011A, _choice(r, [72, 180, 300, 96]), 1)
    add_rational(0x011B, _choice(r, [72, 180, 300, 96]), 1)
    # ResolutionUnit (0x0128) 2=inches, 3=cm
    add_short(0x0128, _choice(r, [2, 3]))

    # Build IFD table
    ifd_entries = bytearray()
    # count
    if order == 'II':
        ifd_entries.extend(struct.pack('<H', len(entries)))
    else:
        ifd_entries.extend(struct.pack('>H', len(entries)))

    # Placeholder: we appended either 12-byte packed entries or tuples needing backpatch
    # We need to know the TIFF base to compute absolute offsets. TIFF base = start of TIFF header in APP1 payload.
    # We'll first compute sizes to find where value_area will be placed.

    # Compute layout sizes:
    # TIFF header (8 bytes) + IFD count (2) + N*12 + nextIFD(4) then value_area
    tiff_header_size = 8
    ifd_table_size = 2 + len(entries) * 12 + 4
    # The value area will start immediately after the IFD table
    value_area_offset = tiff_header_size + ifd_table_size

    # Now serialize entries, backpatching offsets for large data
    for e in entries:
        if isinstance(e, bytes):
            ifd_entries.extend(e)
        else:
            tag, fmt, count, start = e
            absolute = value_area_offset + start
            ifd_entries.extend(_pack_ifd_entry(order, tag, fmt, count, absolute))
    # Next IFD offset = 0 (no more IFDs)
    if order == 'II':
        ifd_entries.extend(struct.pack('<I', 0))
    else:
        ifd_entries.extend(struct.pack('>I', 0))

    # Build TIFF blob
    # IFD0 offset points immediately after TIFF header (at byte 8)
    tiff = bytearray()
    tiff.extend(_build_tiff_header(order, 8))
    tiff.extend(ifd_entries)
    tiff.extend(value_area)

    # Wrap into APP1 Exif
    app1_payload = b"Exif\x00\x00" + bytes(tiff)
    # APP1 marker FF E1 and 2-byte length includes the length bytes themselves
    total_len = len(app1_payload) + 2
    if total_len > 0xFFFF:
        app1_payload = app1_payload[:0xFFFD]  # ensure fits
        total_len = len(app1_payload) + 2
    app1 = b"\xFF\xE1" + struct.pack('>H', total_len) + app1_payload

    # Minimal JPEG with SOI and EOI enclosing APP1
    jpeg = b"\xFF\xD8" + app1 + b"\xFF\xD9"
    return jpeg

# Simple TIFF value-area builders for get_/set_ helpers

def _build_numeric_area(r: random.Random, min_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce a small buffer at least min_len with random bytes; also try structured little/big-endian patterns
    patterns = []
    # Zeroes
    patterns.append(b"\x00" * min_len)
    # All 0xFF
    patterns.append(b"\xFF" * min_len)
    # Incrementing bytes
    patterns.append(bytes((i % 256 for i in range(min_len))))
    # Decrementing bytes
    patterns.append(bytes(((min_len - 1 - i) % 256 for i in range(min_len))))
    # Random
    patterns.append(bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(min_len)))
    base = _choice(r, patterns)
    # Occasionally extend beyond min_len up to 32 bytes
    if _rand(r, 0, 1) == 1:
        extra = _rand(r, 0, 24)
        base += bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(extra))
    return base

# Top-level generator

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a scenario:
    #  - 50%: full JPEG with EXIF APP1 (drives exif_loader_write and exif_data_new_from_data/load_data)
    #  - 30%: raw EXIF/TIFF APP1 without SOI/EOI (still plausible for memory loaders expecting EXIF chunk)
    #  - 20%: small numeric buffers for get_/set_ primitives (2,4,8 bytes)
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        blob = _build_min_exif(r)
        # Randomly truncate or pad harmless segments to vary sizes while keeping validity
        # We avoid corrupting structure; optionally append COM marker or padding
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            com = b"\xFF\xFE" + struct.pack('>H', 2 + 6) + b"gen\x00\x00\x00\x00"
            blob = blob[:-2] + com + blob[-2:]  # insert before EOI
        return blob[:4096]
    elif choice < 0.8:
        # Standalone APP1 EXIF block (without JPEG SOI/EOI)
        block = _build_min_exif(r)
        # Strip SOI/EOI leaving APP1
        # block = FF D8 | APP1... | FF D9
        if len(block) > 4 and block[0:2] == b"\xFF\xD8" and block[-2:] == b"\xFF\xD9":
            block = block[2:-2]
        return block[:4096]
    else:
        # Primitive buffer case: choose size among {2,4,8} and emit structured content
        size = _choice(r, [2, 4, 8])
        buf = _build_numeric_area(r, size)
        return buf[:4096]

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# We need to generate valid/interesting binary files for functions:
# - exif_loader_write_file: reads EXIF-relevant data from a file path
# - exif_data_new_from_file: parses EXIF from a JPEG file path
# Both benefit from valid JPEG files with EXIF (APP1) segments, with varying byte orders and tag sets.
# We'll synthesize small but valid JPEG files containing a JFIF/EXIF APP1 with a minimal TIFF IFD
# and some tags. We ensure structural correctness so libexif can parse them.
# Limit total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# JPEG with EXIF layout (high level):
# SOI (FFD8)
# APP1 (FFE1) length, payload starts with "Exif\x00\x00"
#   TIFF header: byte order ("II" or "MM"), 0x002A, 32-bit offset to 0th IFD from start of TIFF header
#   0th IFD: count (2 bytes), entries, next IFD offset (4 bytes)
#   value data area as needed (for ASCII strings etc.)
# Optionally include EXIF IFD pointer tag (0x8769) that points to a second IFD containing a few EXIF tags
# End with EOI (FFD9). We can also add minimal image data segment (SOS ... EOI) but not required for exif parsing.
# Many parsers only need APP1; still, include SOI/EOI for exif_data_new_from_file which expects JPEG.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Helpers to pack values with given byte order

def pack16(v: int, be: bool) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H" if be else "<H", v & 0xFFFF)

def pack32(v: int, be: bool) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I" if be else "<I", v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

class TiffBuilder:
    def __init__(self, be: bool):
        self.be = be
        self.entries: List[Tuple[int,int,int,int]] = []  # (tag, type, count, value_or_offset)
        self.data_blobs: List[bytes] = []  # extra data stored after IFD

    def add_short(self, tag: int, vals: List[int]):
        typ = 3  # SHORT
        cnt = len(vals)
        if cnt == 1:
            packed = pack16(vals[0], self.be) + (b"\x00\x00")
            self.entries.append((tag, typ, cnt, int.from_bytes(packed, 'big')))
        else:
            blob = b"".join(pack16(v, self.be) for v in vals)
            off = self._add_blob(blob)
            self.entries.append((tag, typ, cnt, off))

    def add_long(self, tag: int, vals: List[int]):
        typ = 4
        cnt = len(vals)
        if cnt == 1:
            self.entries.append((tag, typ, cnt, vals[0]))
        else:
            blob = b"".join(pack32(v, self.be) for v in vals)
            off = self._add_blob(blob)
            self.entries.append((tag, typ, cnt, off))

    def add_ascii(self, tag: int, s: str):
        typ = 2
        data = s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
        cnt = len(data)
        if cnt <= 4:
            # store in value field right-justified little/big? TIFF stores raw bytes; we'll pack into 4 bytes
            vbytes = data.ljust(4, b"\x00")
            v = int.from_bytes(vbytes, "big")
            self.entries.append((tag, typ, cnt, v))
        else:
            off = self._add_blob(data)
            self.entries.append((tag, typ, cnt, off))

    def add_rational(self, tag: int, num: int, den: int):
        # type 5 RATIONAL unsigned
        typ = 5
        cnt = 1
        blob = pack32(num, self.be) + pack32(den, self.be)
        off = self._add_blob(blob)
        self.entries.append((tag, typ, cnt, off))

    def add_exif_ifd_pointer(self, exif_ifd_offset_placeholder: int):
        # Tag 0x8769, type LONG, count 1, value is offset to EXIF IFD
        self.entries.append((0x8769, 4, 1, exif_ifd_offset_placeholder))

    def build(self) -> bytes:
        # Build TIFF header + IFD0 + optional EXIF IFD pointed to by a reserved blob if present
        be = self.be
        header = (b"MM" if be else b"II") + pack16(0x2A, be) + pack32(8, be)  # IFD0 starts at offset 8
        # We'll build IFD0 first. Need to compute offsets relative to start of TIFF header.
        entries = list(self.entries)
        # Sort entries by tag for realism
        entries.sort(key=lambda e: e[0])
        ifd0 = pack16(len(entries), be)
        # Placeholder to compute data area start: header (8 bytes) + 2 + n*12 + 4
        data_start = 8 + 2 + len(entries)*12 + 4
        cur_off = data_start
        out_entries = b""
        # We need to map any value fields that require offsets (where stored as offsets to blobs)
        # First, gather blobs and remember their final offsets
        blobs = []
        for tag, typ, cnt, val in entries:
            if self._is_offset_field(typ, cnt, val):
                # schedule blob placement; val holds temporary offset index into data_blobs list
                idx = val  # we stored actual absolute offset here already in _add_blob as relative; rebuild mapping later
            # nothing else needed here
            pass
        # Recompute offsets: we stored blobs in self.data_blobs in order; place them sequentially
        blob_offsets: List[int] = []
        cur = cur_off
        for blob in self.data_blobs:
            blob_offsets.append(cur)
            cur += len(blob)
        # Now write entries, substituting offsets where needed
        for tag, typ, cnt, val in entries:
            if self._is_offset_field(typ, cnt, val):
                # val stored index into data_blobs
                idx = val
                off = blob_offsets[idx]
                value_field = pack32(off, be)
            else:
                value_field = self._pack_value_field(typ, cnt, val, be)
            out_entries += pack16(tag, be) + pack16(typ, be) + pack32(cnt, be) + value_field
        next_ifd = pack32(0, be)
        # Build blob area
        blob_area = b"".join(self.data_blobs)
        return header + ifd0 + out_entries + next_ifd + blob_area

    def _is_offset_field(self, typ: int, cnt: int, val: int) -> bool:
        # We encode offset-needed entries by storing val as the index into data_blobs (small int),
        # but need a sentinel to distinguish. We'll store such val as a small non-negative and keep
        # a parallel map in order of addition. Simpler: make _add_blob return index, and we treat any
        # value >= 0x100000000 as impossible; but integers are unlimited. We'll tag indices by storing
        # negative Python int, but here val is used only internally. We'll instead store the index directly
        # and detect by presence in a set. Maintain range by keeping a dict of seen indices.
        # To avoid complexity, we will reserve a high-bit flag by storing index in Python int and mark via typ 0.
        # However typ must be real. Better approach: store an out-of-band structure mapping id() of tuple.
        # Simpler: we redesign _add_blob to return the index and we will, at write time, assume that for types
        # that cannot fit in 4 bytes or cnt>1 or (typ==2 and cnt>4) we treat val as blob index.
        if typ == 2:
            return cnt > 4
        if typ in (3, 4) and cnt > 1:
            return True
        if typ == 5:
            return True
        return False

    def _pack_value_field(self, typ: int, cnt: int, val: int, be: bool) -> bytes:
        if typ == 3 and cnt == 1:
            return pack16(val, be) + b"\x00\x00"
        if typ == 4 and cnt == 1:
            return pack32(val, be)
        if typ == 2 and cnt <= 4:
            # val encodes bytes big-endian; convert back to 4 bytes
            return val.to_bytes(4, 'big')
        # Otherwise should have been offset field
        return pack32(0, be)

    def _add_blob(self, blob: bytes) -> int:
        idx = len(self.data_blobs)
        self.data_blobs.append(blob)
        return idx


def build_exif_app1(be: bool, with_exif_ifd: bool, include_thumbnail_tags: bool, rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    tb0 = TiffBuilder(be)
    # Basic mandatory-ish tags for IFD0
    # ImageWidth (SHORT), ImageLength (SHORT)
    width = rnd.choice([64, 320, 640, 1024])
    height = rnd.choice([48, 240, 480, 768])
    tb0.add_short(0x0100, [width])
    tb0.add_short(0x0101, [height])
    # Make, Model (ASCII)
    tb0.add_ascii(0x010F, rnd.choice(["ACME", "Canon", "Nikon", "PhoneCam"]))
    tb0.add_ascii(0x0110, rnd.choice(["ModelX", "D90", "EOS", "Ultra"]))
    # Orientation (SHORT)
    tb0.add_short(0x0112, [rnd.choice([1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8])])
    # XResolution, YResolution (RATIONAL)
    tb0.add_rational(0x011A, 72, 1)
    tb0.add_rational(0x011B, 72, 1)
    # ResolutionUnit (SHORT) 2=inches, 3=cm
    tb0.add_short(0x0128, [rnd.choice([2,3])])

    exif_ifd_bytes = b""
    if with_exif_ifd:
        # We'll construct a separate EXIF IFD and append to the blob area, then point to it
        tb_exif = TiffBuilder(be)
        # ExifVersion (ASCII length 4), store as UNDEFINED usually, but ASCII is acceptable for many parsers
        tb_exif.add_ascii(0x9000, "0231")
        # DateTimeOriginal (ASCII)
        tb_exif.add_ascii(0x9003, rnd.choice(["2020:01:02 03:04:05", "2019:12:31 23:59:59"]))
        # SubSecTimeOriginal (ASCII)
        tb_exif.add_ascii(0x9291, rnd.choice(["123", "5"]))
        # ExposureTime (RATIONAL), FNumber (RATIONAL)
        tb_exif.add_rational(0x829A, 1, rnd.choice([30,60,125,250]))
        tb_exif.add_rational(0x829D, rnd.choice([28,32,45,56]), 10)
        # ISOSpeedRatings (SHORT, count=1)
        tb_exif.add_short(0x8827, [rnd.choice([100,200,400,800])])
        exif_ifd_bytes = tb_exif._build_standalone_ifd()
        # Append EXIF IFD bytes as a blob in tb0 and point tag 0x8769 to it
        exif_off_idx = tb0._add_blob(exif_ifd_bytes)
        # For the pointer entry, we use type LONG cnt=1 and will substitute actual offset
        tb0.entries.append((0x8769, 4, 1, exif_off_idx))

    if include_thumbnail_tags:
        # Minimal thumbnail-related tags in IFD0 for robustness (values dummy)
        tb0.add_long(0x0201, [200])  # JPEGInterchangeFormat (offset to thumbnail) - arbitrary within file
        tb0.add_long(0x0202, [1000]) # JPEGInterchangeFormatLength - arbitrary

    tiff_bytes = tb0.build()
    app1_payload = b"Exif\x00\x00" + tiff_bytes
    app1_len = len(app1_payload) + 2  # length field includes its own two bytes
    if app1_len > 0xFFFF:
        # Should not happen with our small data; truncate if needed
        app1_payload = app1_payload[:0xFFFD]
        app1_len = len(app1_payload) + 2
    app1 = b"\xFF\xE1" + pack16(app1_len, True) + app1_payload
    return app1

# Extend TiffBuilder with a helper to build a standalone IFD (entries + next=0 + blobs), returning bytes

def _tb_build_standalone_ifd(self: TiffBuilder) -> bytes:
    be = self.be
    entries = list(self.entries)
    entries.sort(key=lambda e: e[0])
    ifd = pack16(len(entries), be)
    data_start = 2 + len(entries)*12 + 4
    # compute blob offsets
    cur = data_start
    blob_offsets = []
    for blob in self.data_blobs:
        blob_offsets.append(cur)
        cur += len(blob)
    out_entries = b""
    for i, (tag, typ, cnt, val) in enumerate(entries):
        if self._is_offset_field(typ, cnt, val):
            idx = val
            off = blob_offsets[idx]
            value_field = pack32(off, be)
        else:
            value_field = self._pack_value_field(typ, cnt, val, be)
        out_entries += pack16(tag, be) + pack16(typ, be) + pack32(cnt, be) + value_field
    next_ifd = pack32(0, be)
    blob_area = b"".join(self.data_blobs)
    return ifd + out_entries + next_ifd + blob_area

# Monkey-patch method
TiffBuilder._build_standalone_ifd = _tb_build_standalone_ifd


def build_minimal_jfif(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Add a small JFIF APP0 for variety
    app0_id = b"JFIF\x00" + bytes([1,1,0,0,1,0,1,0,0])  # version 1.1, no density, 0x00 thumbnail
    app0 = b"\xFF\xE0" + struct.pack(">H", len(app0_id)+2) + app0_id
    return app0


def build_jpeg_with_exif(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    be = rnd.choice([True, False])
    with_exif_ifd = rnd.choice([True, False])
    include_thumb = rnd.choice([True, False])
    soi = b"\xFF\xD8"
    app0 = build_minimal_jfif(rnd) if rnd.random() < 0.7 else b""
    app1 = build_exif_app1(be, with_exif_ifd, include_thumb, rnd)
    # Minimal scan to satisfy JPEG structure; a tiny dummy scan
    # Define a minimal baseline DQT/DHT/SOF0/SOS sequence would be large; instead many EXIF loaders
    # don't require full image data. But exif_data_new_from_file expects a JPEG; include SOS + EOI minimal chunk.
    # We'll add a COM segment and go to EOI.
    com_text = rnd.choice([b"Created by generator", b"EXIF test"])[:60]
    com = b"\xFF\xFE" + struct.pack(">H", len(com_text)+2) + com_text
    eoi = b"\xFF\xD9"
    jpeg = soi + app0 + app1 + com + eoi
    if len(jpeg) > MAX_SIZE:
        jpeg = jpeg[:MAX_SIZE-2] + eoi
    return jpeg


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose among several variants to cover behaviors
    choice = rnd.random()
    if choice < 0.8:
        data = build_jpeg_with_exif(rnd)
    else:
        # Also produce EXIF-only (no JPEG wrapper) in rare cases, some loaders accept raw EXIF
        be = rnd.choice([True, False])
        app1 = build_exif_app1(be, with_exif_ifd=True, include_thumbnail_tags=False, rnd=rnd)
        # Prepend SOI to keep JPEG context
        data = b"\xFF\xD8" + app1 + b"\xFF\xD9"
    # Ensure size limit
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]
